newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arboyne names CEO to head Nonoc.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arboyne names CEO to head Nonoc.

text.p: Australian mining junior Arboyne NL said on Wednesday it had appointed Steve Kesler as its chief executive officer to help advance its plan to reopen the long-idled Nonoc nickel refining complex in the Philippines.
Arboyne said Kesler's term of employment was for three years and that he would live in Manila.
For the last two years, Kesler has been the chief executive of Compania Minera Dona Ines de Collahuasi in Chile.
He also previously worked for the former RTZ Corp Plc, now called RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, for 17 years.
Nonoc was once one of the world's 10 biggest nickel refineries, capable of producing up to 65 million pounds of metal a year.
But low metal prices and high energy costs coupled with a devalued Philippine peso and high interest rates forced the plant to close in 1986.
Arboyne estimates it will cost about US$370 million to rehabilitate the operation.

Arboyne's resource estimate of recoverable ore remaining at Nonoc and adjacent to the 60 hectare refinery was 39 million tonnes containing an average of 1.28 percent nickel, 0.12 percent cobalt and 38.2 percent iron, the company said.

Arboyne's entry to the project is through its option to acquire Pacific holdings Ltd, a company that acquired Philinco Mining and Industrial Corp, which has concluded an agreement with the Philippines government for the purchase of Nonoc.
